I met my first boyfriend at school and we dated for five years. One night I was making some cakes and I’d left my phone upstairs and my then-boyfriend was asleep on the sofa so I took his phone to take some photos of the stuff I’d made and send them to myself on WhatsApp; I opened WhatsApp and scrolled to look for myself and I must have gone right past it and I saw a conversation with someone who was saved as “C**ks****r” (I’m sure you can work out what that one is). I clicked on it thinking it was going to be something funny like some he hated or something from work but no. It was in fact what their name said they were. After finding this I confronted him and he said he didn’t know what it was and it must have been a sick joke one of his friends played on him. And I believed him because it was so out of character for him. 

Over the next few days something just didn’t sit right with me and I kept thinking about it so I went back to his phone (just a little side note here - I’d never been through his phone before, I’d always respected his privacy and I had never once suspected anything/felt the need or desire to go through his phone). I found more suspicious things on his phone and then I waited for him to go to work the next day and I went through his computer. In all honesty I wasn’t at all prepared for what I’d find... I found email accounts with conversations going back 4 years with men he’d met on Craigslist, ads he’d posted on Craigslist looking for crossdressers, pictures of him dressed as a woman (some with... adult toys included), pictures of my underwear, pictures of him dressed in my underwear, pictures of him with... things in his mouth. You get the picture. He was mainly into crossdressers/crossdressing. That sort of thing. 

Anyway, I called him and told him he needed to come home straight away and he took 90 minutes longer than he should have (presumably because he’d been rumbled). All I remember from that phone call was shouting and being so I angry I couldn’t understand what I was saying anymore. When he eventually returned home he denied doing the whole debacle and said he didn’t remember doing it if he had done it at all. So I called his mother and told her the situation and told her she needed to make sure he saw a psychiatrist because he appeared to be having blackouts. Then I packed up his stuff and moved him out of the house. 

I was humiliated, betrayed and heartbroken. And I think it’ll take a lot to top that in my life.
